Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- The failing test wraps a Base32-encoded string in a ByteArrayInputStream, then wraps that in a Base32InputStream. It then performs a skip (omitted in the snippet but implied by the comment “due to CODEC-130, skip now skips correctly decoded characters rather than encoded”) and expects that reaching the end of the decoded stream makes the next read() return -1.
- The current bug report for Base64InputStream.skip describes the same symptom: skip operates on the underlying encoded stream rather than on the decoded output stream. Base32InputStream and Base64InputStream share the same base class for streaming codec I/O, so the same root cause would affect both.
- Inspecting the implementation shows:
  - Base32InputStream is a thin wrapper over BaseNCodecInputStream with a Base32 codec, constructed via super(in, new Base32(...), doEncode).
  - BaseNCodecInputStream overrides read() and read(byte[], int, int) to decode via the BaseNCodec instance, but it does not override skip().
  - BaseNCodecInputStream extends FilterInputStream (it calls super(in) in its constructor). FilterInputStream.skip(long n) delegates directly to the underlying stream’s skip(n) without going through the decoder.
- As a result, calling skip(n) on Base32InputStream (or Base64InputStream) skips raw encoded bytes in the wrapped InputStream, not n decoded bytes from the decoded output. This violates the intent captured in the test comment referencing CODEC-130 (skip should skip decoded characters).
- Consequences observed in the test:
  - The test attempts to skip to the end of the decoded stream and then asserts that read() returns -1.
  - Because skip bypasses the decoder, it does not necessarily consume the decoded output. Depending on the encoded/decoded length relationship, data may remain decodable after the skip, so a subsequent read() returns a byte instead of -1, causing the test to fail.
- This same root cause explains the Base64InputStream.skip() issue in the bug report: skip counts and consumes bytes in the underlying encoded stream rather than the decoded output, returning unexpected values and leaving data available to be read afterward.

In short: BaseNCodecInputStream does not override skip(), so it inherits FilterInputStream.skip(), which skips the underlying encoded stream. For Base32InputStreamTest.testSkipToEnd(), this means skip does not consume decoded data to EOF, so read() does not return -1 as expected. The fix is to implement skip(long) in BaseNCodecInputStream to discard decoded bytes (e.g., by repeatedly reading into a buffer) so that skip counts and behavior reflect decoded output.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
